issuer: the Department of Vehicle and Drivers' Licensing (DVDL)
note: Read 2026-10-30 on the DVDL's site. The Traffic Act (2026 Revision, revised as at 31 December 2025): no one is qualified to drive unless of the prescribed age for the group of vehicle (s 25(a)(i)) and has passed the written and road tests (s 37(1)); the licence is issued on the certificate of competence and the prescribed fee (s 38) and stays in force three, five or ten years according to the period for which the fee is paid (s 41(1)). The Traffic Regulations (2026 Revision), reg 6(1)(a): a person of at least seventeen may drive a motor car (driver's licence groups 1 and 2), so the full licence is held from 17 (the learner's licence needs the same age and a written test, and there is no minimum time on it). The DVDL's press release of 31 August 2026 sets the fees from 1 September 2026, by whether the holder is Caymanian: a full driver's licence for groups 0–3 costs CI$25 (non-Caymanian CI$75) for one year, CI$68 (225) for three, CI$106 (375) for five and CI$200 (750) for ten. The ten-year licence, the Act's longest term, is held, with the non-Caymanian's fee as foreignFee: the form's citizen is read as a Caymanian here (Caymanian status, which DVDL verifies, isn't citizenship alone). The learner's licence (CI$60/120) and the tests aren't held. No identity card of DVDL's is held; the Driving Licences Exchangeable Order 2021 wasn't read, so no exchange list is held. From 2026-10-30 (the lead, when the form took a non-citizen's fee for each term) the licence holds the four terms the release sells, 1, 3, 5 and 10 years, each with its Caymanian and non-Caymanian fee; until then it held the ten-year licence alone.
